spatial_claims.claim: Points A, C, B are collinear on a straight line with C between A and B, so AC is the remainder AB - BC
II.7 applied to line AB cut at C: AB^2 + BC^2 = 2*rect(AB,BC) + AC^2

configuration_map: Trivial linear configuration: three collinear points A, C, B on a single straight line, with C between A and B. No triangles, circles, angles, or complex geometric figures are constructed. The entire proof operates on algebraic properties of areas (rational, medial, commensurable) derived from this line segment.
skip_reason: The proof is essentially purely algebraic, dealing with commensurability and rationality/irrationality of areas. The only geometric element is the identity II.7 applied to a line segment cut at a point — a trivially simple collinear configuration with no possibility of spatial contradiction. No triangles, circles, angle decompositions, interior/exterior arguments, or ray orderings appear. This is a typical Book 10 irrationality proof with no meaningful geometric configuration to check.
